title: Master Service Level Agreement
body:
# Master Service Level Agreement

**Norvane Managed IT Services Oy** ("Norvane") and the Customer named in the
applicable Service Schedule ("Customer").

Version 4.2, effective 1 January 2025. Replaces version 3.6 (2021-11-02).

## 1. Purpose and structure

This Master Service Level Agreement ("Master SLA") sets out the framework terms
under which Norvane delivers managed IT services. It does not by itself commit
Norvane to any specific performance level. The committed performance levels for
each Customer are set out in that Customer's **Service Schedule**, which
incorporates this Master SLA by reference.

The following documents form part of the agreement, in descending order of
precedence:

1. The Customer's Service Schedule
2. This Master SLA
3. The Service Credit and Penalty Policy (DOC-005)
4. The Support Tier Definitions (DOC-006)
5. Norvane's published operational policies, as amended from time to time

Where a Customer's Service Schedule and this Master SLA conflict, the Service
Schedule prevails for that Customer only.

## 2. Definitions

**Service Availability** — the percentage of minutes in a calendar month during
which a covered service is operational and able to perform its documented
function, excluding Excused Downtime.

**Excused Downtime** — downtime arising from: (a) a Customer-approved
Maintenance Window notified at least five (5) business days in advance;
(b) Customer-side faults including but not limited to Customer-owned equipment,
Customer network changes made without Norvane involvement, or Customer staff
actions; (c) Force Majeure; (d) suspension for non-payment.

**Severity** — P1 to P4 as defined in DOC-006.

**Recovery Time Objective (RTO)** — the maximum acceptable elapsed time from
declaration of a disaster to restoration of the service at the agreed
functional level.

**Recovery Point Objective (RPO)** — the maximum acceptable age, measured
backwards from the time of failure, of the most recent recoverable copy of data.

**Business Hours** — 07:00 to 18:00 EET/EEST, Monday to Friday, excluding
Finnish public holidays.

## 3. Service tiers

Norvane offers four service tiers: **Platinum**, **Gold**, **Silver** and
**Bronze**. The tier assigned to each Customer is stated in its Service
Schedule. Tier determines the committed availability target, the P1 response
and resolution obligations, the recovery objectives and the maximum service
credit percentage. Support tier definitions (P1–P4) are common to all tiers;
the tier determines the clock against which response and resolution are
measured.

## 4. Measurement and reporting

Availability is measured by Norvane's monitoring platform (DOC-021) using
synthetic probes at one-minute intervals, supplemented by device up/down traps.
Measurement methodology is not negotiable per Customer except where a Service
Schedule explicitly specifies an alternative probe set.

Where monitoring data is unavailable or disputed, the parties shall use the
ticketing system's recorded timestamps as the system of record.

Monthly service reports are issued within five (5) business days of month end
and state, per covered service: availability achieved, incident counts by
severity, P1 response and resolution performance, and any credit due.

## 5. Service credits

Service credits are the Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for failure to
meet a committed service level. The credit schedule, calculation method, caps
and claim procedure are set out in DOC-005. Credits are applied against the
following month's invoice and are not payable in cash.

## 6. Exclusions

Norvane is not responsible for performance of services, applications or
connectivity not supplied by Norvane, including Customer-owned WAN links,
third-party SaaS applications and Customer-managed on-premises systems, except
where a Service Schedule explicitly extends coverage.

## 7. Term, termination and review

Initial term and renewal terms are stated in each Service Schedule. Either
party may terminate for material breach with thirty (30) days' written notice
and a fifteen (15) day cure period. This Master SLA is reviewed annually by
Legal & Compliance; the current review date is shown in the document metadata.

## 8. Change control

Amendments require written agreement of both parties. Norvane may amend
operational policies referenced in clause 1 without Customer consent provided
the amendment does not reduce a committed service level.

# Service Schedule — Aurora Health District

Customer: **Aurora Health District** (CUST-01)
Tier: **Platinum**
Effective: 2025-11-20. Supersedes v1.4 dated 2021-04-01.
Contract term: 2021-04-01 to 2027-03-31, renewal by 12 months unless cancelled
with 90 days' notice.

## 1. Covered services and committed levels

| Service | Committed level |
|---|---|
| Network & Connectivity | 99.95% monthly availability |
| Backup & Recovery | RTO 4 hours, RPO 1 hour |
| Managed Firewall | P1 response 15 minutes, P1 resolution 4 hours |
| Service Desk | P1 response 15 minutes, 24x7 |

Availability is measured across the three covered sites (aurora-hq,
aurora-clinic, aurora-archive) and reported in aggregate, not per site.

## 2. Site coverage

| Site | Address | Circuits |
|---|---|---|
| aurora-hq | Hallituskatu 12, Helsinki | 2 x 200 Mbit/s Vantage Fibre, diverse paths |
| aurora-clinic | Rautatienkatu 4, Tampere | 1 x 100 Mbit/s Vantage Fibre |
| aurora-archive | Vanha talvitie 9, Helsinki | 1 x 50 Mbit/s Vantage Fibre |

## 3. Clinical systems carve-out

Patient record systems hosted by the District's application provider are
**not** covered by this Schedule. Norvane's responsibility ends at the
network demarcation to the application provider's environment. Where a fault
in the covered network causes loss of access to a clinical system, the incident
is nonetheless treated as P1 and the clock in section 1 applies.

## 4. Backup and recovery

The District's backup scope covers file services, directory services and
configuration data on Norvane-managed infrastructure. Clinical application
data is backed up by the application provider and is out of scope.

Committed objectives: **RTO 4 hours, RPO 1 hour**, measured from declaration
of a disaster. Norvane performs a restore test of the file service tier at
least twice per year; the District may witness one test per contract year.

## 5. Reporting and review

In addition to the standard monthly report, Norvane provides a quarterly
service review attended by the District's IT lead and clinical operations
representative. Aurora receives incident notification for all P1 and P2
incidents by telephone within the response window, followed by email.

## 6. Regulatory obligations

Norvane acknowledges that the District operates under Finnish health data
regulation and the EU GDPR. Personnel with access to District data hold
criminal-record clearance for social and health care work. All access is
logged and reviewed quarterly. Data classification for District material is
Confidential at minimum; clinical data is Restricted (see DOC-025).

## 7. Service credits

Maximum credit: 30% of the monthly fee for the affected service. The credit
schedule in DOC-005 applies without amendment; the Platinum escalator in
section 3 of that policy applies.

## 8. Special terms

Clause 9.2 of the Master SLA's annual review procedure is waived; review is
quarterly. Termination for convenience requires 90 days' notice and a
documented transition plan.

# Service Schedule — Cobalt Retail Group

Customer: **Cobalt Retail Group** (CUST-03)
Tier: **Gold**
Effective: 2025-06-30. Supersedes v2.2.
Contract term: 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31.

## 1. Covered services

| Service | Committed level |
|---|---|
| Network & Connectivity | 99.9% monthly availability |
| Backup & Recovery | RTO 8 hours, RPO 4 hours |
| Managed Firewall | P1 response 30 minutes, P1 resolution 8 hours |
| Service Desk | P1 response 30 minutes, 24x7 |

## 2. Site coverage

Six sites: cobalt-hq (Helsinki) and five retail stores (cobalt-store-01 to
cobalt-store-05). Stores connect to HQ over site-to-site VPN on consumer-grade
fibre; store-level availability is measured but the **committed** availability
target applies to the aggregate across all six sites.

Because retail trading hours dominate the risk profile, availability is
measured over **trading hours only** (08:00–21:00 local, seven days) rather
than the full calendar month. This is an explicit amendment to the Master SLA
definition of Service Availability and applies to Cobalt only.

Store openings and closures during the contract term are handled by a site
variation notice rather than a Schedule amendment, provided the total site
count does not exceed eight.

## 3. Peak trading periods

Cobalt designates four peak trading periods per year (roughly November,
December, January sale and a summer promotion). During these periods:

- No planned maintenance on core or distribution switching without written
  approval from Cobalt's IT manager.
- P1 response target is reduced to 15 minutes by mutual agreement.
- A Norvane duty engineer is on site at cobalt-hq during the first trading day
  of the period.

The current peak period calendar is maintained by the Service Delivery Manager
and is not part of this Schedule.

## 4. Core switching

Cobalt operates a two-switch stack at HQ (see DOC-012 for the configuration
standard). Redundancy is expected to survive the loss of one member. The
Schedule does not commit to a specific failover time; the availability target
is the only committed measure.

## 5. Backup scope

File services, POS transaction logs, HQ directory services. POS databases are
backed up by the POS vendor; Norvane retains the vault copy and is responsible
for restoring the vault copy only.

## 6. Reporting

Monthly report plus a quarterly review with head of IT and store operations.

## 7. Service credits

Maximum credit 20% of the monthly fee for the affected service. Because
availability is measured over trading hours, credit calculations use
trading-hour minutes as the denominator.

## 8. Special terms

Cobalt may request up to two emergency change windows per quarter at no charge.
Additional emergency windows are chargeable at the rates in the rate card.

title: Service Credit and Penalty Policy
body:
# Service Credit and Penalty Policy

This policy operationalises clause 5 of the Master SLA (DOC-001). It applies to
all Customers with an active Service Schedule.

## 1. Principle

Credits are compensation for missed commitments, not a penalty. They are
automatic where monitoring data proves the miss, and are capped per Service
Schedule. Credits are applied to the next invoice; they are never paid in cash
and never exceed the cap.

## 2. Availability credits

Credits are calculated per service per calendar month from achieved
availability:

| Availability achieved vs target | Credit (% of monthly fee for service) |
|---|---|
| Within 0.05 pp of target | 0% |
| 0.05 to 0.20 pp below | 5% |
| 0.20 to 0.50 pp below | 10% |
| 0.50 to 1.00 pp below | 20% |
| More than 1.00 pp below | 30%, capped per Schedule |

"pp" means percentage points. A Silver customer at 99.5% target achieving
99.31% is 0.19 pp below target and receives 5%.

## 3. Platinum escalator

Where a Platinum Customer misses its availability target in two consecutive
months, the second month's credit is doubled before applying the cap. Where
three consecutive months are missed, the Customer may terminate the affected
service without penalty on 30 days' notice.

## 4. Response and resolution credits

A missed P1 response is credited at 2% of the monthly fee for the affected
service per occurrence, to a maximum of 10% in any month. A missed P1
resolution is credited at 5% per occurrence, to a maximum of 15%. Response and
resolution credits are cumulative with availability credits but subject to the
single overall cap in the Service Schedule.

## 5. Claims procedure

Norvane raises credits automatically from the monthly service report. A
Customer disputing the report must raise the dispute within fifteen (15)
business days of the report date. Disputes are resolved by the Service Delivery
Manager; unresolved disputes escalate to the account director.

Customers do not need to claim availability credits. Credits arising from
events where monitoring data is incomplete must be claimed explicitly.

## 6. Worked example

Eastgate Housing Association (Bronze, 99.0% target) suffered a 6 hour 40
minute outage in June 2026 caused by the upstream provider (INC-2026-0128).
Trading/measured window was the full calendar month. Achieved availability was
98.7%, which is 0.3 pp below target → 10% bracket, but the Bronze cap is 5%,
so the credit issued was 5% of the monthly connectivity fee, EUR 3,100.

The upstream provider's own credit to Norvane for the same event was EUR 1,850
under the Vantage Fibre SLA (DOC-007). Norvane does not pass through upstream
credits; the Schedule's cap governs.

## 7. Exclusions

No credit is due for downtime classified as Excused Downtime under DOC-001
clause 2, or for incidents caused by a Customer action taken contrary to
Norvane's written advice.

title: Support Tier Definitions (P1-P4)
body:
# Support Tier Definitions (P1–P4)

## 1. Severity matrix

| Severity | Definition | Typical examples |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Complete loss of a covered service, or loss affecting patient safety, statutory reporting or all trading locations. No workaround. | Core switch down; site offline; backup restore fails during a declared disaster |
| **P2** | Major degradation of a covered service, or loss affecting a significant subset of users with no acceptable workaround. | One store offline; firewall blocking a business-critical SaaS application; 30–70% of users unable to work |
| **P3** | Degradation with an acceptable workaround, or a single user or small group affected. | Port flapping; one user's VPN broken; print queue stuck |
| **P4** | Cosmetic, informational, or a request for change rather than a fault. | Documentation correction; capacity question; cosmetic UI issue |

Severity is set by Norvane at triage and may be re-graded with the Customer's
agreement. A Customer may request an upgrade to P1; the duty manager decides
within 30 minutes and records the decision on the ticket.

## 2. Response and resolution clocks

The clock starts when the ticket is created in the ITSM system, not when the
Customer notices the fault. For telephone-reported incidents, the clock starts
at call answer.

Committed values are per Customer tier and are held in the `sla_targets` table.
The generic framework is:

| Tier | P1 response | P1 resolution | P2 response | P3 response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platinum | 15 min | 4 h | 30 min | 4 h |
| Gold | 30 min | 8 h | 1 h | 8 h |
| Silver | 60 min | 12 h | 2 h | 1 business day |
| Bronze | 4 business hours | 24 business hours | 4 business hours | 2 business days |

**Response** means a qualified engineer has engaged, acknowledged the
incident to the Customer and begun diagnosis. An automated acknowledgment does
not stop the clock.

**Resolution** means the service is restored to its documented function. A
workaround agreed with the Customer stops the resolution clock but opens a
linked P3 problem ticket.

## 3. Escalation triggers

Automatic escalation to the duty manager occurs when:

- a P1 is unacknowledged at 50% of the response window
- a P1 remains unresolved at 75% of the resolution window
- a P1 has more than three Customer chase contacts
- three or more P1s are open simultaneously

Further escalation paths are in DOC-020.

## 4. Downgrade rules

A P1 is downgraded to P2 only when the service is restored or when the
Customer and the duty manager agree that the fault is narrower than first
reported. Downgrade does not retroactively remove the response-clock
commitment.

## 5. Out-of-hours behaviour

Platinum and Gold Customers are supported 24x7 for P1 and P2. Silver and
Bronze are supported in business hours; a P1 raised out of hours pages the
on-call rota, but P2 and below are queued until the next business day.

## 6. Common errors at triage

- Classifying a single-user VPN fault as P2 instead of P3 inflates the
  reporting and creates false breaches.
- Classifying a store outage as P3 during peak trading is a recurring
  disagreement with Cobalt; the peak-period terms in DOC-004 section 3 govern.
- Recording the Customer's "first noticed" time as the open time distorts the
  response metric.

title: Network Architecture Overview
body:
# Network Architecture Overview

## 1. Purpose and scope

This document provides the authoritative overview of Norvane Managed IT Services Oy's network architecture. It describes the physical layout, logical topology, and inter-site connectivity for the two data centres (DC1 Helsinki and DC2 Tampere) as well as the upstream circuits that provide internet and MPLS access. The scope covers all equipment in the data centre and edge network. Customer site architectures are documented separately in the individual site plans.

The primary audience is the infrastructure team, the service desk, and any engineer who must understand the network for incident response or change management.

## 2. Physical topology

DC1, the primary data centre, is located in Pasila, Helsinki. It houses six VMware vSphere 8 ESXi hosts, two core switches operating in a StackWise virtual pair, a border router, an edge firewall pair, and a VPN concentrator. Power is delivered through dual PDUs fed by separate UPS circuits with backup generator support.

DC2, the disaster recovery site, is located in Kaleva, Tampere. It contains three vSphere 8 hosts, a single Catalyst 9300-48P access switch (core-sw-11), and the termination point for the DC1-to-DC2 L2 circuit. DC2 has no local internet breakout — all internet-bound traffic from DC2 backhauls to DC1 over the L2 tunnel carried by the VF-HEL-4473 circuit.

## 3. Logical topology and VLANs

The logical topology follows the VLAN plan defined in DOC-011. Each site uses the standard VLAN set: 10 (Data), 20 (Voice), 30 (Corporate Wi-Fi), 40 (Guest Wi-Fi), 50 (Print/IoT), 60 (CCTV, retail and plant sites only), 99 (Management), and 999 (Transit).

The transit VLAN 999 connects DC1 and DC2 over the L2 circuit and carries inter-site traffic only. The Management VLAN 99 runs to all network devices, including the border router, firewalls, core switches, and ESXi management interfaces.

At DC1 the core is built around two Cisco Catalyst 9500-48Y4C switches in StackWise virtual mode (core-sw-01 / core-sw-02). The Cisco ASR 1001-X border router (core-rtr-01) sits upstream of the FortiGate 400F edge firewall pair (fw-edge-01 and fw-edge-02). The FortiGate 201F VPN concentrator (vpn-conc-01) handles all remote-access and site-to-site tunnels.

## 4. Data centre interconnect

DC1 and DC2 are connected via the Vantage Fibre circuit VF-HEL-4473, a 1 Gbit/s L2 link carrying VLAN 999. This circuit provides the transport for all DC2 inter-site traffic, including management, replication, and server traffic.

Upstream connectivity terminates at DC1 only. The primary circuit (VF-HEL-4471) delivers 1 Gbit/s symmetric, with the backup circuit (VF-HEL-4472) providing 300 Mbit/s up / 100 Mbit/s down as a fallback. Internet and cloud access flows through the firewall pair at DC1.

## 5. Resilience and redundancy

DC1 employs a fully redundant core design: the StackWise virtual pair on the Catalyst 9500s provides link-level and device-level redundancy, and the FortiGate 400F edge pair runs active-active with automatic failover. The border router connects to both core switches for upstream diversity.

DC1 and DC2 sit on geographically diverse fibre paths with no shared physical infrastructure. The two sites are connected over separate right-of-way routes, eliminating any single-point-of-failure risk in the transport layer between them.

DC1 hosts six ESXi nodes; the cluster can tolerate the loss of two hosts while maintaining full workload coverage. DC2's three hosts provide sufficient capacity for failover of the most critical workloads.

## 6. Known limitations

The current design has the following constraints:

- DC2 uses a single Catalyst 9300-48P switch (core-sw-11) with no redundancy at the access layer. A failure of core-sw-11 takes the entire DR site offline.
- DNS resolution in both DC1 and DC2 depends on the same two domain controllers located at DC1. No local DNS resolvers exist at DC2.
- No traffic engineering exists between the primary (VF-HEL-4471) and backup (VF-HEL-4472) upstream circuits; failover is controlled solely by the edge firewalls.
- DC2 has no local internet connectivity. If the L2 backhaul to DC1 fails, DC2 workloads lose all external access.

## 7. Document control

| Version | Date       | Author             | Change summary |
|---------|------------|--------------------|----------------|
| 6.0     | 2026-05-04 | Marko Heinänen     | Updated firmware baselines and host counts; clarified DC2 backhaul design |
| 5.0     | 2024-08-15 | Marko Heinänen     | Added DC2 Catalyst 9300 detail; aligned with DR plan v3.0 |
| 4.0     | 2022-01-10 | Marko Heinänen     | Major revision after migration to vSphere 8 |
| 3.0     | 2019-06-20 | Ilkka Rantala      | Initial DC2 site description |

# IP Addressing and Subnet Plan

## 1. Purpose

This document is the authoritative record of Norvane's IP address block allocation, VLAN plan, and named infrastructure addresses. Every subnet assigned to a customer site, internal service, or infrastructure component must be recorded here before it is configured on any device. Assets.csv and all other inventory systems derive their network data from this plan.

## 2. Address block allocation

Norvane's IP plan uses RFC 5737 documentation ranges (198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24, 192.0.2.0/24) as the plan of record. The allocation is as follows:

| Block | Use |
|---|---|
| 198.51.100.0/26 | DC1 management (VLAN 99) |
| 198.51.100.64/26 | DC1 server VLAN 10 |
| 198.51.100.128/26 | DC1 DMZ |
| 198.51.100.192/26 | Transit VLAN 999 |
| 203.0.113.0/26 | DC2 management |
| 203.0.113.64/26 | CUST-05 dunmore-hq |
| 203.0.113.128/26 | CUST-06 eastgate |
| 192.0.2.0/26 | CUST-01 (aurora-hq, aurora-clinic) |
| 192.0.2.64/26 | CUST-02 (brambleby-hq, brambleby-depot) |
| 192.0.2.128/26 | CUST-03 (cobalt-hq + stores) |
| 192.0.2.192/26 | CUST-04 (feldspar) |

## 3. Site addressing

DC1 (Pasila, Helsinki) uses the 198.51.100.0/25 block, subdivided into four /26 subnets for management, servers, DMZ, and the transit VLAN. DC2 (Kaleva, Tampere) uses the 203.0.113.0/26 management block; customer sites at this address space are served directly from the /24.

Customer management addresses are drawn from the 192.0.2.0/24 block. Each customer receives one /26, subdivided further per site as needed. The final /26 of each customer's allocation is reserved for future growth and must not be assigned to active services.

## 4. VLAN standard

The following VLAN identifiers are used across all sites unless a schedule explicitly states otherwise:

| VLAN | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | Data | General data traffic |
| 20 | Voice | VoIP / SIP trunks |
| 30 | Corporate Wi-Fi | Staff wireless network |
| 40 | Guest Wi-Fi | Visitor wireless network |
| 50 | Print/IoT | Printers and IoT devices |
| 60 | CCTV | CCTV (retail and plant sites only) |
| 99 | Management | Network device management |
| 999 | Transit | DC inter-site transit |

## 5. Named infrastructure addresses

| Device | Address | Site |
|---|---|---|
| core-rtr-01 | 198.51.100.11 | DC1 |
| core-sw-01 | 198.51.100.12 | DC1 |
| core-sw-02 | 198.51.100.13 | DC1 |
| fw-edge-01 | 198.51.100.21 | DC1 |
| fw-edge-02 | 198.51.100.22 | DC1 |
| vpn-conc-01 | 198.51.100.23 | DC1 |
| bkparr-01 | 198.51.100.41 | DC1 |
| core-sw-11 | 203.0.113.31 | DC2 |
| bkparr-02 | 203.0.113.42 | DC2 |

## 6. Allocation conventions

Static IP assignment is used exclusively for network infrastructure devices and servers. DHCP reservations are applied to printers, CCTV cameras, and AP controllers — end-user devices receive dynamic addresses from the site-level pool.

No NAT is performed at customer sites. All customer subnets use documentation-range addressing as recorded in this plan. Every new subnet must be recorded here before any configuration takes place.

## 7. Recently reclaimed space

The range 192.0.2.32/27 was assigned to aurora-archive before that customer moved into the CUST-01 block (192.0.2.0/26) in February 2026. The old range is now quarantined and will remain unassigned until at least 2027. Do not reuse this range during the quarantine period.

## 8. Change control

All changes to this plan — new subnets, reallocations, or removals — must be submitted as a change request (CHG-YYYY-NNNN) and recorded in the Confluence page listed in the frontmatter. The IP address plan is owned by Marko Heinänen (Head of Infrastructure).

title: Core Switch Configuration Standard
body:
# Core Switch Configuration Standard

## 1. Scope

This standard defines the gold-image configuration baseline for all Cisco Catalyst switches in the Norvane managed network. It applies to Catalyst 9500 (core), Catalyst 9300 (distribution), and Catalyst 9200 (access layer) platforms. Any switch that is part of the core or distribution fabric must conform to this document unless a formal exception is on file.

## 2. Firmware baseline

The supported firmware baseline for core and distribution switches is IOS-XE 17.9.4a. Access layer switches may run 17.6.5 where full 17.9.x support is not yet available on the target platform.

Two access layer devices are currently outside the supported baseline and are flagged for upgrade:
- The eastgate-offices access switch (running 17.3.8)
- The brambleby-depot access switch (running 17.3.8)

These devices are noted in DOC-041's asset register and must be upgraded to at least 17.6.5 as part of the next maintenance window. Until upgraded, they carry an open exception under this document.

## 3. Base configuration

All switches are configured from a common gold image that sets the following defaults:

- Hostname in the format `site-role-NN` (e.g. dc1-core-01)
- DNS domain set to `norvane.internal`
- NTP synchronised from internal sources only — no public NTP servers
- Syslog directed to the central collector on the management VLAN
- Banner displaying the Norvane security notice on all login banners
- HTTP server disabled; only HTTPS (TLS 1.2 or later) for management access
- CDP and LLDP both enabled globally for interoperability

## 4. Spanning tree and link aggregation

Rapid PVST+ is the spanning tree protocol across all VLANs. An explicit root bridge is configured per VLAN: core-sw-01 is the primary root for all data VLANs, and core-sw-02 is the secondary root. Bridge priority is set explicitly rather than relying on MAC address as the tiebreaker.

Uplinks to the access layer are bundled into LACP port-channels with the switchport in `mode active` (active-only; PAgP is not used). Access layer switchports accept LACP port-channels and reject PAgP.

Jumbo frames (MTU 9000) are enabled on the transit VLAN (999) only. All other VLANs use the standard 1500-byte MTU. This ensures no fragmentation of inter-site replication traffic while avoiding compatibility issues on standard access ports.

## 5. Management plane

Management access follows these rules:

- SNMPv3 is the only supported SNMP version. SNMPv2c is explicitly prohibited on all switchports.
- NTP sources are internal only; the NTP server at DC1 provides time synchronisation to all switches.
- Syslog is forwarded to the central collector. Local logging is retained at debugging level for a rolling 72-hour window.
- The management VLAN (99) is the sole VLAN permitted for out-of-band and in-band management traffic.
- HTTPS is enabled for GUI access; HTTP is disabled across all ports.

## 6. Access control

- TACACS+ is used for all administrative authentication. Per-user accounts are required; shared or group accounts are prohibited.
- Exactly one break-glass local account exists per device. Its credential lives in the vault and is used only when TACACS+ is unavailable. Access via this account triggers an immediate alert to the security team.
- Unused switchports are administratively shut down and parked in a blackhole VLAN (VLAN 9999) to prevent unauthorized device attachment.
- Port security is enabled on all user-facing ports with a maximum of two MAC addresses and shutdown action on violation.

## 7. Configuration backup

The running configuration is backed up to the vault (//fs01.norvane.internal/vault/switch-configs/) after every change. The backup process is triggered automatically through the change management system and also runs as a cron job every six hours. Configuration diffs are generated and compared against the previous backup to detect unauthorized or unrecorded changes.

## 8. Baseline deviations

Any deviation from this gold image — including custom VLANs, non-standard spanning tree settings, or alternative authentication methods — must be documented in a change request with full justification. Approved deviations are recorded as exceptions in this document. No deviation is permissible without an associated change ticket.

## 9. Exceptions

Exceptions require written approval from the Head of Infrastructure and expire after 90 days. Expired exceptions must be renewed or the non-compliant configuration must be reverted. The current exception covering the eastgate-offices and brambleby-depot access switches (IOS-XE 17.3.8) expires on 2026-06-30 and must be renewed if upgrades cannot be completed in the planned maintenance window.

title: Firewall Change Management Policy
body:
# Firewall Change Management Policy

## 1 Purpose

This policy governs all changes to firewall rules on Norvane's FortiGate 400F edge pair (fw-edge-01, fw-edge-02), Catalyst core zone-firewalls, and VPN concentrator policies. Firewall changes carry high risk — a single mis-ordered rule can expose internal services or break customer traffic. Every change must be authorised, tested, peer-reviewed, and documented before touching production.

## 2 Scope

This policy applies to every modification of a firewall rule — additions, deletions, source/destination/port changes, and rule reordering — on edge firewalls, core switch zone policies, and VPN concentrator rules. Firmware upgrades and interface changes are excluded (DOC-012, DOC-024). All Norvane personnel with firewall write access, external contractors managing firewall objects, and the security engineering team are subject to this policy.

## 3 Change classes

**Standard changes** are pre-approved, recurring modifications affecting no more than five ports. They are logged as tickets with no CAB approval required, but must be peer-reviewed by a second security engineer before implementation.

**Normal changes** cover all other modifications: new destination networks, changes affecting more than five ports, any internet-facing rule, and any change altering a customer-facing service scope. Normal changes require CAB approval, a written rollback plan, and five business days' lead time.

**Emergency changes** must be implemented immediately to resolve an active security incident, critical outage, or compliance breach. They follow a fast-tracked approval path (see §9) and are subject to retrospective CAB review.

## 4 Approval and the CAB

Normal and emergency changes require CAB approval. The CAB meets weekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 EET. Standing members are the Security Lead, the Head of Infrastructure, the Service Delivery Manager, and a rotating Service Desk representative.

The CAB reviews each ticket for impact analysis, rollback feasibility, timing, and peer-review confirmation. Peer review by a second security engineer is mandatory before the ticket reaches the CAB; the reviewer's initials and date must appear on the ticket. Changes affecting more than five ports or any internet-facing rule require CAB sign-off and cannot be handled as standard changes.

## 5 Lead time and scheduling

Normal changes require five business days' lead time between CAB approval and implementation. A business day is 07:00–18:00 EET/EEST, Monday–Friday, excluding Finnish public holidays. Insufficient lead time means deferral to the next CAB meeting unless the change qualifies as an emergency.

Implementation windows for normal changes are scheduled on Tuesdays or Thursdays during 18:00–22:00 EET unless the CAB authorises an alternative window.

## 6 Testing and rollback

A written rollback plan is mandatory before CAB approval. The plan must identify every rule to be added, modified, or reordered, specify the exact reversal action, and state the expected post-rollback state.

Changes must be tested in the staging environment (or in a non-production rule ordering on fw-edge-02) before implementation. Test results must be recorded on the ticket. Changes that break connectivity during testing require a revised rollback plan and renewed CAB approval.

## 7 Post-change verification

After implementation, the engineer runs a verification test: connectivity checks from source to destination on every affected port. A 30-minute observation window follows. The ticket stays open during this window; any issue triggers immediate rollback. The ticket closes only after the window passes cleanly.

## 8 Rule lifecycle and review

Every edge firewall rule is reviewed every six months for business need, scope accuracy, and compliance. Rules with zero hits over a 12-month period are marked for removal — a notice is added to the rule description and removal occurs at the next change window. A final review of recent traffic confirms no burst or seasonal traffic is being overlooked.

Monitoring and alert thresholds supporting firewall reviews are defined in DOC-021.

## 9 Emergency changes

Emergency changes may be approved by the Security Lead together with the on-duty manager. Approval must be verbal or via synchronous communication; email alone is insufficient. The emergency ticket must be raised within 24 hours and must include a retrospective description, justification, and full rollback plan. Retrospective review occurs at the next CAB meeting. Emergency changes follow the same post-change verification and observation window as normal changes.

## 10 Records

All firewall change tickets are retained in the ITSM system for a minimum of three years. Records include the ticket number, change class, approval status, CAB minutes, peer review confirmation, rollback plan, verification results, and observation log. Emergency records also include the emergency justification and the retrospective CAB assessment. Service tier definitions for incident response are in DOC-006.

title: Firewall Change Management Policy
body:
**Version 1.0 — superseded by version 3.0. Retained for audit purposes.**

# Firewall Change Management Policy

## 1 Purpose

This document sets out the procedure for making changes to firewall rules on Norvane's perimeter and internal firewalls. All firewall modifications must be documented and approved before they are applied to any production device. The purpose of this policy is to maintain a controlled, auditable change process while keeping the team's ability to respond to business needs flexible and fast.

This policy was created as part of the migration to the new FortiGate estate, which is currently being rolled out across both data centres. It replaces the previous rule-change procedure documented in the earlier version of this file.

## 2 Scope

This policy applies to all changes on the firewall devices managed by the network team of four. Changes include additions, deletions, and modifications of any rule, whether on the edge firewalls or on internal zone-firewall policies. Changes to firewall firmware, interface configuration, or general device settings are not covered by this document — those fall under the infrastructure change procedure.

All members of the network team, the service desk, and any external contractors with firewall access are subject to this policy.

## 3 Change categories

Changes are divided into two categories:

**Standard changes.** These are routine, low-risk modifications that follow a documented and pre-approved procedure. Examples include adding a single destination IP to an existing allow rule, updating a port range within an already-approved service group, and removing a source address that was previously authorised by the Network Manager. Standard changes are logged as tickets but do not require further approval beyond the ticket record.

**Non-standard changes.** Any change that does not qualify as standard is non-standard. This includes the creation of entirely new rules, changes to internet-facing rules, and modifications that affect multiple customer services. Non-standard changes must be approved by the Network Manager before implementation.

## 4 Approval procedure

All non-standard changes require written approval from the Network Manager (Ilkka Rantala). Approval is obtained by email. The change request must be sent to the Network Manager at least 48 hours before the intended implementation date. The email must describe the change, the business reason, the scope of affected rules, and the engineer responsible for implementation.

The Network Manager will respond with approval, a request for more information, or a rejection. If more information is needed, the 48-hour clock restarts from the date of the Network Manager's reply. If the Network Manager is unavailable, the duty network engineer may provisionally approve a non-standard change and notify the Network Manager as soon as possible thereafter.

Standard changes do not require email approval but must be recorded on a change ticket with the implementing engineer's name and a description of the work performed.

## 5 Lead time

A minimum of 48 hours' notice is required for all non-standard changes. This means that the change request email must be sent to the Network Manager at least two business days before the intended implementation date. Changes requested on shorter notice will be deferred to the next available window unless the situation qualifies as an emergency.

Implementation of firewall changes is scheduled on a best-effort basis and is carried out during the evening maintenance window or, where urgent, during business hours with the approval of the Network Manager. The network team aims to have all non-standard changes implemented within ten business days of the Network Manager's approval, subject to operational priorities.

## 6 Testing

Changes should be tested before they are applied to production devices where practicable. The network team maintains a test firewall instance where rule ordering and rule content can be validated. If a suitable test instance is not available, changes must be implemented in a way that allows immediate rollback — typically by placing new rules below existing allow rules in the rule order and verifying connectivity before removing any deny rules.

No rollback plan is required for changes submitted under this policy. The implementing engineer is expected to retain the ability to revert any change immediately in the event of an unexpected impact.

## 7 Post-change verification

After a change is implemented, the implementing engineer should verify that the change works as expected and that no unintended traffic is now passing. This verification is informal and does not require a formal test procedure. Any issues identified during verification should be addressed before the change ticket is closed.

## 8 Rule review

All firewall rules are reviewed quarterly as part of the network team's routine maintenance. During the quarterly review, rules that have not carried traffic for more than six months are flagged for removal. The network team will also check for overlapping rules and redundant entries during the review.

The Network Manager is responsible for sign-off on any rule removals identified during the quarterly review.

## 9 Emergency changes

In the event of an emergency — for example, a critical security vulnerability that must be mitigated by closing a port, or a service outage caused by a firewall rule — the network team may apply a change immediately and notify the Network Manager by phone or email as soon as possible. The Network Manager will confirm the change in writing within 24 hours. Emergency changes are logged on a change ticket with a description of the emergency and the action taken.

## 10 Records

All firewall change tickets are retained in the ITSM system. Records include the ticket number, the category of change, the approval record (email or ticket note), and a description of the work performed. Ticket records are available to members of the network team and to the Service Desk for reference.

title: VPN and Remote Access Guide
body:
# VPN and Remote Access Guide

## 1 Scope

This guide covers remote access to Norvane's network services via the site-to-site and remote-user VPN infrastructure. It describes the VPN concentrators, client software, authentication, session policies, split tunnelling rules, contractor-specific procedures, common troubleshooting scenarios, and support boundaries. This guide applies to all personnel who connect using the remote-user VPN and to the service engineers who manage the concentrators.

The VPN infrastructure does not grant unrestricted network access. The tunnel carries business traffic only. Access to management interfaces on network devices is outside the scope of this guide and is governed by DOC-041.

## 2 Client software and profiles

The standard VPN client for all Norvane users is FortiClient, using IPsec IKEv2. The client is deployed to all employee endpoints via the configuration management system, and to contractor endpoints on a case-by-case basis after security screening.

There is a single VPN gateway address, presented to users as vpn.norvane.internal. The gateway is load-balanced across two FortiGate 201F concentrators located at DC1 Helsinki (vpn-conc-01 as primary, vpn-conc-02 as secondary in active/passive mode). Users do not configure the gateway address directly; FortiClient resolves it automatically.

Portal profiles are configured per customer. Each customer profile is named after the customer's short name (for example, aurora, cobalt, feldspar) and contains the customer-specific address pools, DNS settings, and access rules. Users are assigned a single profile based on their employment relationship or contractor agreement. The profile determines which internal networks the user can reach after the tunnel is established.

## 3 Authentication

Authentication is performed against Microsoft Entra ID using SAML as the primary factor. All users authenticate with their corporate credentials through the SAML assertion flow. FortiClient handles the SAML exchange transparently; the user sees only the standard Microsoft login prompt.

When SAML is unavailable — for example, due to an Entra ID outage or a network condition that prevents the SAML redirect — TOTP serves as the fallback factor. TOTP is configured through the Norvane mobile authentication application. The TOTP code is entered manually into FortiClient after the primary SAML attempt fails. Fallback to TOTP is automatic; the user is not required to request it.

Multi-factor authentication is mandatory on every VPN profile. There are no exceptions. Both the SAML + TOTP combination and the standalone TOTP fallback satisfy the MFA requirement. Password-only access is never granted.

## 4 Session policy

The maximum session lifetime is 10 hours. After 10 hours of continuous connection, the VPN session is terminated and the user must re-authenticate. This applies to all users and all profiles regardless of customer tier or role.

The idle timeout is 30 minutes. If a user is inactive on the VPN for 30 minutes or more, the session is dropped. The user must re-authenticate to reconnect. Active sessions are identified by sustained traffic through the tunnel; users who leave sessions open without activity are expected to be re-authenticated by the idle timeout.

Sessions are logged in the concentrator's authentication log and forwarded to the SIEM for monitoring. Session records include the user identity, the customer profile, the timestamp, and the source IP address.

## 5 Split tunnelling

Split tunnelling is permitted only for the profiles listed in the approved allow-list, which is maintained by the security engineering team and referenced in the concentrator configuration. The allow-list identifies the specific customer profiles for which the user's local network traffic is not required to traverse the VPN tunnel.

For all profiles not on the allow-list, full tunnelling is enforced. This means that all IP traffic from the client is routed through the VPN tunnel to the destination network. Split tunnelling is not available for contractor profiles, for emergency access profiles, or for any profile that grants access to the management VLAN.

The allow-list is reviewed quarterly by the security engineering team. Changes to the allow-list must be approved by the Security Lead.

## 6 Contractor access

Contractors connecting via the VPN are subject to additional security requirements beyond those applied to employees. Before the VPN tunnel is established, FortiClient performs a posture check on the contractor device. The posture check verifies three conditions:

1. Disk encryption is active (BitLocker on Windows, FileVault on macOS).
2. The operating system is at or above the minimum patch level defined in the current patch standard.
3. A supported antivirus agent is installed, active, and up to date.

If any one of these checks fails, the tunnel is not established. Instead, the user is redirected to the remediation page, which provides instructions and the download links for the required software or configuration steps. The user may retry the connection after the remediation steps are complete.

Contractor VPN sessions are subject to the same session and idle timeouts as employee sessions. Contractor access is reviewed monthly by the service delivery team and is revoked automatically when the contractor agreement expires.

## 7 Troubleshooting

The following are the most commonly encountered VPN issues and their standard resolutions:

**Stale DNS after a customer move.** When a customer relocates to a new IP range and the address pool is updated, FortiClient may retain the old DNS entries in its cache. The user sees intermittent name resolution failures for previously reachable hosts. The standard resolution is to disconnect and reconnect the VPN, or to run the client DNS flush command. If the issue persists after reconnection, the concentrator's DNS settings should be verified against the customer's current IP plan in DOC-011.

**MTU or MSS problems on IPsec.** Users report that some web pages load incompletely or that large file transfers hang. This is typically caused by the IPsec encapsulation reducing the effective MTU below what the application expects. The standard resolution is to set the MSS clamping value on the VPN interface to match the minimum MTU of the tunnel path, or to enable automatic MTU discovery on the client profile.

**Expired client certificate.** FortiClient uses a device certificate for the initial IKE exchange. If the device certificate has expired — for example, after a device rebuild — the connection fails with an authentication error. The standard resolution is to request a new certificate through the certificate management portal and reinstall it on the device via the configuration management system.

**Locked AD account.** After multiple failed login attempts, the user's Active Directory account is locked and VPN authentication fails. The standard resolution is for the user to unlock the account through the self-service password reset portal or by contacting the service desk. After unlocking, the user reconnects the VPN.

**Profile mismatch after a customer site change.** When a customer adds or removes sites, the VPN profile may no longer match the user's expected access. The user reports missing resources or unexpected access to previously unreachable networks. The standard resolution is to verify the user's profile assignment in the concentrator configuration against the current site-to-profile mapping and to refresh the profile on the client if required.

## 8 Support boundaries

The service desk handles initial VPN connectivity triage: verifying the user's account status, confirming the VPN client is running, and testing basic authentication. Escalation to the network or security engineering teams is required when the issue involves concentrator configuration, profile assignment, or posture check failures.

Administrative access to network devices via the VPN is explicitly prohibited. Administrators must use the bastion host and the privileged access path defined in DOC-041. Any attempt to access management VLANs or management interfaces through the VPN tunnel is logged and may result in account suspension pending review.

title: DNS and DHCP Standards
body:
# DNS and DHCP Standards

## 1 Scope

This standard defines the architecture, configuration, and operational procedures for DNS and DHCP services across Norvane's data centres and all managed customer sites. It covers internal authoritative zones, external authoritative zones, dynamic and static address assignment, and the DHCP options that must be consistent across all scopes.

This standard applies to all DNS servers, DHCP servers, and configuration management tools used to administer these services. It covers both the internal infrastructure DNS/DHCP and the per-customer scope configurations. Changes to DNS zone transfers, DHCP scope parameters, or option templates must follow the procedures in this document.

## 2 DNS architecture

Internal DNS zones are authoritative on Windows Server AD-integrated DNS. Two domain controllers host the internal zones with automatic multi-master replication via Active Directory. All client devices, application servers, and network devices resolve internal names through the domain controllers.

External authoritative zones are served by BIND. The BIND instances respond to queries from the internet for Norvane's public domains. Zone data for external zones is updated independently of the AD-integrated internal zones.

Both domain controllers forward non-authoritative queries to the internal resolvers, which in turn forward unresolved queries to the ISP resolvers provided by Vantage Fibre. The forwarder chain is: client → local DC → internal resolver → ISP resolver → internet. Internal resolvers cache aggressively to reduce external queries.

DNS scavenging is enabled on all dynamic records. The scavenging interval is seven days: records that are not refreshed within seven days are considered stale and are removed during the next scavenging cycle. Scavenging is not enabled on static records; static records persist until explicitly deleted by a network administrator.

## 3 Record management

A-record and AAAA-record creation must follow a documented naming convention. Hostnames for managed devices use the convention defined in the IP addressing plan (DOC-011). Customer device records are created per the customer-specific schedule and naming rules documented in the onboarding package.

PTR records are maintained for all addresses in the management, server, and DMZ subnets. PTR records for the data VLANs are maintained on a best-effort basis and are not guaranteed to be present for all DHCP-assigned addresses.

DNS zone transfers are enabled between the two AD-integrated domain controllers and between the BIND primary and secondary. No external zone transfer is permitted; only the configured secondary BIND instance receives zone data.

All DNS record changes must be logged in the configuration management system. Manual changes to zone files on the BIND servers require approval from the infrastructure lead and must be performed during a maintenance window.

## 4 DHCP architecture

DHCP service is split 80/20 between the two domain controllers. DC1 operates the primary DHCP scope with an 80% address range; DC2 operates the secondary scope with a 20% address range. A delay of 120 seconds is configured on the DC2 instance to prevent duplicate lease assignments during initial service start-up.

The DHCP split is applied uniformly across all customer site scopes and the Norvane internal scopes. Customer site DHCP scopes are hosted on the local domain controllers at each site where a DC is deployed. Sites without a local domain controller use the Norvane internal DHCP scopes and receive addresses from the DC1/DC2 pool.

DHCP reservations are used for printers, CCTV cameras, and Wi-Fi controllers. Reserved addresses are configured in the DHCP server console and are consistent across all sites that share the same VLAN IDs. Reservation records include the device type, the MAC address, the assigned IP, and the customer or site identifier.

## 5 Option standards

The following DHCP options are applied to every scope unless a documented exception exists:

- Option 003 (default gateway): The gateway for the VLAN's subnet.
- Option 006 (DNS servers): The two domain controller addresses.
- Option 015 (domain name): The internal DNS domain suffix.
- Option 042 (NTP servers): The primary and secondary NTP server addresses.
- Option 043 (vendor-specific information): The VoIP handset boot server address. This option is applied only to the Voice VLAN scope.
- Option 119 (domain search list): The DNS search suffixes for the internal domain and the customer domains listed in the onboarding package.

All scopes must include options 003, 006, 015, 042, and 119. Option 043 is optional and is applied only where VoIP handsets are in use. Scope parameters and option values are managed through the configuration management system; manual changes to the DHCP server console are prohibited except in emergency recovery scenarios.

Lease times are set as follows:
- Data VLANs: 8 days.
- IoT VLANs: 30 days.
- Management VLAN: leases are not issued; see exclusions below.

## 6 Exclusions

No DHCP service is provided on management VLAN 99. All addresses on the management VLAN are static. Management IP addresses are assigned manually from the management subnets defined in the IP addressing plan (DOC-011) and recorded in the asset inventory.

Customer sites that have only a single layer-2 switch and no local DHCP relay are covered by the Norvane internal DHCP scopes. The DHCP relay agent (IP helper) on the customer edge device forwards requests to the DC1 primary. No scope is created on the customer premises.

## 7 Known weaknesses

The following items are documented here for awareness. Resolution is deferred until resources are available:

- No quarterly review of stale static records is currently performed. Static records that are no longer associated with active devices accumulate in the zone files over time. The next scheduled review is to be included in the upcoming infrastructure audit cycle.
- Split-scope exclusions — the address ranges where the 20% secondary DC is excluded from issuing leases — are maintained by hand in a spreadsheet whose location is recorded nowhere in this document. The spreadsheet must be migrated into the configuration management system as part of the next standards revision.
- Scavenging is disabled on two legacy scopes that are still in use for the Brambleby Logistics and Eastgate Housing sites. These scopes were originally created before scavenging was standardised and have not been updated. The scopes are targeted for replacement during the next VLAN restructuring initiative.

title: Wireless Standards
body:
# Wireless Standards

## 1. Scope

This document defines the wireless networking standards for Norvane Managed IT Services Oy. It applies to all wireless infrastructure owned or operated by Norvane, including sites hosted for customers under the Aurora Health District and Feldspar Manufacturing service agreements.

## 2. Controller platform

Wireless management uses Cisco Catalyst 9800-series controllers in HA pairs: one pair per data centre. DC1 (Helsinki Pasila) runs the primary controller; DC2 (Tampere Kaleva) holds a standby pair to maintain SSID broadcasts and roaming state during a DC1 outage. Controllers are on management VLAN 99.

## 3. SSID design

Three SSIDs are provisioned across all managed sites:

- **norvane-corporate** — WPA2-Enterprise with 802.1X authentication against Active Directory. Users authenticate with domain credentials; devices use machine auth via Cisco ISE posture profiling. Maps to VLAN 30.
- **norvane-guest** — Pre-shared key with a captive portal for end-user registration. Rate-limited to 50/10 Mbit/s per user. Maps to VLAN 40 and is subject to content filtering.
- **norvane-iot** — WPA2-PSK with MAC filtering enforced by ISE. Reserved for printers, sensors, and POS devices. Maps to VLAN 50 with restricted ACLs permitting only necessary outbound endpoints.

Band steering is enabled to direct 802.11n/ac/ax-capable clients to 5 GHz. The 2.4 GHz band is retained for legacy devices.

## 4. Security

The corporate SSID uses 802.1X with EAP-PEAP-MSCHAPv2. TKIP is not permitted; CCMP/AES is required. The guest SSID uses a shared PSK rotated quarterly through change management and stored in the vault. The IoT SSID uses MAC filtering as an additional layer; MAC addresses alone are not sufficient for high-security zones.

WPA3 is not currently enabled. WPA3 'will be enabled during 2022 once the controller firmware upgrade completes'.

## 5. Radio design

Design targets: minimum RSSI −67 dBm at the client for data services, −60 dBm for voice-over-Wi-Fi. Sites use Cisco Prime WIPS for predictive heat-mapping before deployment.

Channel planning: 5 GHz at 40 MHz width; 2.4 GHz at 20 MHz on channels 1, 6, and 11 only. Transmit power is auto-adjusted via the RF Profile (18–22 dBm). Dynamic RF is enabled for channel and power optimisation.

## 6. Site survey process

A predictive or validated site survey is required for every new site before AP placement is signed off. Deliverables include a floorplan with AP locations, expected RSSI coverage, and channel assignments. No AP procurement order is raised until the survey is approved by the Head of Infrastructure.

## 7. AP inventory

Access points are deployed per site as follows:

| Site | AP count |
|---|---|
| aurora-hq | 14 |
| cobalt-hq | 9 |
| feldspar-plant | 11 |
| brambleby-hq | 6 |
| dunmore-hq | 4 |
| eastgate-offices | 5 |

All access points are Cisco Catalyst 9115-series (2×2:MIMO, 802.11ac Wave 2).

## 8. Roadmap

The Wi-Fi 6 rollout 'is planned for Q3 2021'. Once AP hardware is in place, WPA3 'will be enabled during 2022 once the controller firmware upgrade completes'. A further review of this document will be carried out after both migrations are complete.

title: Backup and Restore Runbook
body:
# Backup and Restore Runbook

## 1. Scope

This runbook covers backup and restore procedures for all Norvane-managed services, including infrastructure-level image backups, file services, and database tiers. It applies to both data centres (DC1 Helsinki, DC2 Tampere) and is intended for use by the Backup & Storage Engineer and Service Desk team during restore operations. Application-level backups performed directly by vendors on database appliances are documented separately.

## 2. Backup infrastructure

Norvane operates two Dell PowerProtect DP4400 appliances:

- **bkparr-01** — deployed at DC1 (Helsinki Pasila), management address 198.51.100.41. Primary appliance handling all local backup jobs.
- **bkparr-02** — deployed at DC2 (Tampere Kaleva), management address 203.0.113.42. Secondary appliance receiving replicated backups from bkparr-01.

Both appliances are connected to management VLAN 99 and managed through the PowerProtect Data Manager web console. Replication between them runs over the dedicated DC1-to-DC2 fibre link.

## 3. Schedule and retention

Image-level backups run nightly between 01:00 and 06:00 EET/EEST. After each successful job on bkparr-01, a replication job is triggered to bkparr-02. No replication starts until the source job is confirmed successful.

Hourly SQL transaction log shipping is enabled where a database is in scope for backup, preserving point-in-time recovery capability between nightly image snapshots.

Retention: 30 daily copies retained locally on bkparr-01; 12 monthly copies for long-term recovery (one per calendar month, retained 12 months). Replicated copies on bkparr-02 mirror the source retention schedule. All data is encrypted at rest with AES-256. Recovery keys are held in the vault and accessible only to the Backup & Storage Engineer and Head of Infrastructure.

## 4. Recovery objectives

Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) per service tier, from DOC-019 section 3:

| Tier | RTO | RPO |
|---|---|---|
| Platinum | 4 h | 1 h |
| Gold | 8 h | 4 h |
| Silver | 24 h | 12 h |
| Bronze | 48 h | 24 h |

## 5. Restore procedures

**Single-file restore from the ProtecTIER file-level index (~20 min):** Log in to the bkparr-01 console, navigate to the target protection policy, open the most recent successful backup and browse the file-level index. Select the required file or directory, then restore to the original location or an alternate path. The console reports progress in real time.

**Whole-volume restore (~2 hours):** On the bkparr-01 console, select the target protection policy and open the most recent backup image. Choose the entire volume or disk. Restore to the original location, or to an alternate host if the source is unavailable. Monitor progress from the Activity dashboard.

**Database restore from log-shipped copy (~3 hours):** Confirm hourly log shipping is configured for the target database. If not, fall back to whole-volume restore. From the bkparr-01 console, select the restore point closest to the desired recovery time. Initiate a restore to the original or a temporary recovery host, then apply the transaction log chain from the log shipping store to reach the selected point in time. Verify the restored database against the application-level checksum.

**Site-level restore by promoting bkparr-02 (~6 hours):** Notify the Service Delivery Manager and Head of Infrastructure. Log in to the bkparr-02 console at DC2 and confirm the replicated backup set is current via the Replication dashboard. Initiate a Site Failover Restore on the target protection policy. Redirect DNS for affected services to DC2 addresses per DOC-019 section 6. Validate replicated data has been applied and services are responding. Coordinate with the Service Delivery Manager for customer notification.

## 6. Testing

Restore tests are performed twice yearly and cover the file-services tier only. Database restores are tested at vendor level, not end to end in the Norvane environment. Tests are recorded in the ITSM system as a problem ticket and closed upon completion.

## 7. Known gaps

- No automated verification of backup integrity beyond job success status. No checksum or data-level validation is performed after each nightly backup.
- Replication lag between bkparr-01 and bkparr-02 is not alerted on. No Zabbix alert exists if replication falls behind by more than 30 minutes.
- No documented procedure for restoring the clinical database tier end to end. Vendor-level restore tests have been conducted but no Norvane-end-to-end runbook exists for this tier.

title: Disaster Recovery Plan
body:
# Disaster Recovery Plan

## 1. Purpose and scope

This plan establishes procedures for recovering Norvane Managed IT Services Oy's services after a disaster at the primary data centre (DC1, Helsinki Pasila). It covers all infrastructure at both DC1 and DC2 (Tampere Kaleva), and the customer sites for which Norvane is responsible for service recovery.

The plan applies to all service tiers defined in DOC-006 and DOC-018. It is owned by the Head of Infrastructure and coordinated with the Service Delivery Manager for customer communications.

## 2. Assumptions

DC2 remains operational and the Vantage Fibre upstream circuit at DC2 is independent of the DC1 failure. Backup replication has kept the DC2 copy within documented RPO targets. Staff can work remotely or at DC2. The network topology in DOC-010 remains valid.

## 3. Recovery objectives

The following RTO and RPO values match the committed targets in DOC-018 section 4 and are validated against the results of the most recent disaster recovery test.

| Tier | RTO | RPO |
|---|---|---|
| Platinum | 4 h | 1 h |
| Gold | 8 h | 4 h |
| Silver | 24 h | 12 h |
| Bronze | 48 h | 24 h |

## 4. Declaration of disaster

A disaster is declared by the Head of Infrastructure jointly with the Service Delivery Manager, when both agree that DC1 cannot deliver services to one or more Customers within the RTO for the affected tier(s). The Service Delivery Manager notifies affected Customers within 1 hour of declaration for Platinum and Gold services, via registered customer contact channels with expected recovery timeline.

The declaration is logged in the ITSM system as a major incident and triggers the escalation procedures defined in DOC-020.

## 5. Recovery sequence

Recovery at DC2 is executed in five ordered phases:

**01 — Networking and remote access.** Confirm DC2 core switching, routing, and upstream Vantage Fibre circuits are operational. Re-establish management and transit VLANs. Ensure VPN concentrators are functional for engineering staff.

**02 — Identity and DNS.** Bring Active Directory domain controllers at DC2 online and verify replication from the latest backup. Restore DNS servers and confirm authoritative zones resolve. Update DHCP scopes if required.

**03 — File services.** Promote the file server cluster at DC2 from the most recent bkparr-02 image. Validate share permissions and confirm file-level restore capability via the ProtecTIER interface.

**04 — Business applications.** Restore application server virtual machines from DC2 backup images. Validate application connectivity to databases and update configuration to point at DC2 endpoints.

**05 — Voice.** Bring VoIP services online at DC2. Verify SIP registration and call routing through the PBX. Confirm phone service is available to end users.

## 6. Data centre failover

On disaster declaration, bkparr-02 at DC2 is promoted as the primary backup and restore target. Replication jobs are redirected to DC2. DNS records for customer-facing services are updated to resolve to DC2 addresses, and traffic is rerouted through the Vantage Fibre circuit at DC2.

DC2 has a known limitation: a single Catalyst 9300-48P switch with no redundant uplinks. During a disaster, this switch becomes the critical path for all DC2-originated traffic.

## 7. Communication and customer notification

The Service Delivery Manager is responsible for all external communications. For Platinum and Gold tier services, an initial update is provided within 1 hour of declaration, followed by updates every 2 hours until services are restored. For Silver and Bronze, an initial notification is sent within 4 hours. All communications include affected services, estimated recovery time, and current status.

## 8. Validation

A full disaster recovery test was carried out on 2024-11-16. All tiers were exercised and all objectives were met. The test confirmed DC2 promotion, DNS failover, and backup restore processes function within documented RTO targets.

Restore testing is performed twice yearly across all backup tiers. The next scheduled test is in May 2026 and will exercise the full recovery sequence as described in section 5.

## 9. Maintenance of this plan

This plan is reviewed every six months or following any incident affecting DC1 or DC2 availability. Changes to network topology, backup infrastructure, or customer tier assignments require an update. The Head of Infrastructure is responsible for maintaining this plan and ensuring all recovery procedures remain current and tested.

title: On-Call and Escalation Policy
body:
# On-Call and Escalation Policy

## 1. Purpose

This policy governs the on-call rota, acknowledgement obligations, and escalation
ladder for Norvane Managed IT Services Oy. It applies to all members of the
Service Desk and Infrastructure teams who participate in the support operation.
Severity classifications follow DOC-006.

## 2. Coverage and rota

Norvane provides 24 × 7 coverage for Platinum and Gold customers for P1 and P2
incidents. Silver and Bronze customers receive support during business hours only
(07:00–18:00 EET/EEST, Monday to Friday, excluding Finnish public holidays); a
P1 raised out of hours pages the on-call rota as a fallback.

The rota is published every Monday by the duty manager and covers 24-hour
calendar shifts. Each shift carries one primary engineer and one secondary
engineer. The primary holds the console; the secondary monitors the queue and
stands ready to assume the primary role if the primary is unavailable.

Shift handover is conducted at 08:00 EET each morning. A written handover record
is posted to the shared Service Desk folder and attached to the corresponding
incident management ticket; see section 6.

## 3. Acknowledgement obligations

Every page or assignment in the Service Desk system must be acknowledged within
15 minutes of receipt. The acknowledgement may be a status change in the ITSM
tool or a voice call to the originating channel.

If the primary engineer fails to acknowledge a page within 15 minutes, the
system automatically pages the secondary engineer on the same shift. A P1 must be
escalated to the duty manager within 15 minutes of ticket creation. The duty
manager records the escalation reason on the ticket and notifies the affected
customer if the response window has been exceeded.

All acknowledgement times are logged in the Service Desk audit trail and form the
basis of the monthly SLA compliance report.

## 4. Escalation ladder

The escalation ladder for incidents is:

1. Duty engineer (primary on-call)
2. Duty manager
3. Head of Infrastructure
4. Service Delivery Manager

The duty manager holds the rota contact sheet. Individual mobile numbers are never
published in this document or in any customer-facing material. If escalation is
required, the duty engineer or secondary contacts the duty manager through the
process described in DOC-023.

The Head of Infrastructure is escalated when the incident affects more than one
data centre or requires a change outside normal maintenance windows. The Service
Delivery Manager is the final escalation point and owns customer communication
throughout the incident.

## 5. Out-of-hours authority

During out-of-hours periods (defined as outside 07:00–18:00 EET/EEST Monday to
Friday, excluding Finnish public holidays), the authority to approve an emergency
infrastructure change rests with the duty manager acting jointly with the
Security Lead. This follows the change management process documented in DOC-013
and supersedes the normal CAB approval requirement for emergency items only.

The duty manager logs the joint approval on the change ticket and obtains formal
CAB sign-off within two business days of the implementation.

## 6. Handover

The handover at 08:00 must include:

- A list of all open P1 and P2 incidents, with current status and any SLA
  countdowns.
- Pending customer callbacks, including the requested callback window and the
  customer tier.
- Any active change freeze, with its scope and the name of the person who
  imposed it.
- Outstanding action items from the previous shift that were not closed.

The outgoing primary and incoming primary both sign the handover record. Any
discrepancy must be resolved before the 08:00 handover concludes.

## 7. Records

All on-call shifts, handover records, escalation events, and acknowledgement times
are retained for a minimum of two years in the Service Desk repository. Quarterly
reviews of the rota coverage are performed by the Service Delivery Manager to
ensure adequate staffing across all tiers.

title: Monitoring and Alert Thresholds
body:
# Monitoring and Alert Thresholds

## 1 Purpose

This document defines the monitoring platform and alert thresholds for Norvane's managed infrastructure. It covers Norvane-owned equipment and customer-premises devices where Norvane operates the monitoring agent. The purpose is to ensure faults are detected within timeframes consistent with DOC-006 and DOC-020.

## 2 Platform and polling

All monitoring is performed through Zabbix. Zabbix polls every monitored device at 60-second intervals for SNMP-based metrics: CPU, memory, interface counters, temperature, power state, and fan status. The poller timeout is set to 55 seconds.

In addition to SNMP polling, Zabbix runs synthetic probes every 60 seconds:
- ICMP reachability checks against every IP in the device register.
- HTTP/HTTPS endpoint checks against VPN concentrator management URLs, verifying application-layer responsiveness.

SNMPv3 traps are accepted from all network devices and both backup appliances; traps bypass the polling interval and are processed immediately.

Syslog from routers, firewalls, switches, and backup appliances is forwarded to the Zabbix syslog receiver at DC1 and correlated against the active trigger table.

## 3 Alert classes and thresholds

The following table defines every alert trigger. Each row maps a condition to a severity and the detection window.

| Condition | Severity | Window |
|---|---|---|
| Link down (any documented interface port) | P1 | Immediate |
| Packet loss above 1 % over 5 minutes on a measured path | P2 | 5 min |
| Round-trip latency above 50 ms sustained for 5 minutes | P2 | 5 min |
| Interface error counters increasing on any uplink (CRC, runts, giants) | P2 | 10 min |
| CPU above 85 % for 10 minutes | P3 | 10 min |
| Memory above 90 % for 10 minutes | P3 | 10 min |
| Disk above 85 % | P3 | 1 poll |
| Power supply failure | P2 | Immediate |
| Fan failure | P2 | Immediate |
| BGP or upstream peer down | P1 | Immediate |
| Hardware temperature above vendor threshold | P2 | Immediate |
| Backup job failed | P2 | Immediate for Platinum/Gold; next morning for Silver/Bronze |
| Switch stack member lost | P1 | Immediate |

Severity grading follows DOC-006. Alerts feed the Zabbix action engine which routes to the on-call rota; de-duplication is applied before a ticket is opened. The Service Desk team lead may re-grade alerts during triage per DOC-006.

The backup-job rule reflects tier differences: Platinum and Gold backups are escalated immediately; Silver and Bronze failures are aggregated into the morning operations review.

## 4 Routing and de-duplication

Alerts route through Zabbix actions to the on-call rota defined in DOC-020, keyed by device asset tag and customer association. Unassigned (Norvane-internal) devices route to the internal infrastructure rota.

De-duplication suppresses repeated alerts for the same device and trigger within 30 minutes; suppressed firings are appended as correlation notes to the existing ticket.

Flapping suppression applies to link and BGP-state events: three state transitions (up/down) within any 10-minute window triggers a dedicated P1 ticket and a 20-minute suppression period. A fourth transition after the suppression window opens a new ticket.

## 5 Maintenance windows

During approved maintenance windows (DOC-022), the ITSM integration marks affected devices in Zabbix as "maintenance mode" at the window start, suppressing all trigger evaluation.

Suppression clears automatically at the window end time. Overruns must be extended in ITSM; cancelled windows require clearance within 15 minutes.

## 6 What is deliberately not alerted

- Replication lag between `bkparr-01` (DC1) and `bkparr-02` (DC2) is collected and displayed on the dashboard but generates no alert. This gap is consistent with DOC-018; the backup schedule pass/fail status is already covered in Section 3.
- Interface error counters on access ports are not alerted. Only uplink counters are monitored per the threshold table.

## 7 Review

Threshold adjustments are submitted as Change Requests per DOC-024.

title: Patching and Maintenance Windows
body:
# Patching and Maintenance Windows

## 1 Purpose

This policy defines the patching cadence and maintenance windows for Norvane's infrastructure. It applies to all network equipment, servers, and appliances managed by Norvane at DC1 (Helsinki) and DC2 (Tampere), as well as customer-premises devices. The purpose is to ensure security and operational patches are applied promptly and consistently, with minimal disruption to customer services.

## 2 Patch cadence

Norvane performs monthly firmware and OS patching on all managed equipment. A quarterly review of the firmware baseline is carried out to evaluate new releases and plan adoption. The current firmware baseline is IOS-XE 17.9.4a on core switches and FortiOS 7.2.9 on edge firewalls, as recorded in DOC-012.

Critical security patches on internet-facing equipment must be applied within 14 days of vendor release. Critical security patches on internal-only systems must be applied within 30 days.

Any patch that cannot be applied within the applicable window becomes a tracked exception. Exceptions are documented in the ITSM system and reviewed quarterly.

## 3 Maintenance windows

The standard maintenance window for all patching and firmware changes is Sunday 01:00–05:00 EET. Windows may be shortened or extended at the discretion of the Head of Infrastructure.

Platinum Customers may have individual maintenance windows agreed in their service schedule. These take precedence over the standard window when they conflict.

Maintenance windows are excluded during peak trading periods for retail Customers. The exclusion periods are defined in DOC-004 section 3 and are applied automatically by the change calendar. No patching work occurs during those periods except under a P1 incident.

## 4 Notification

The Service Desk sends notification to every customer's nominated technical contact and copies the notification to the Service Desk mailbox. A standard maintenance window is announced at least 5 business days before the window start. A change to the firmware baseline (i.e. a version update not covered by the current quarterly review) requires 10 business days' advance notice.

Notifications include the affected equipment, the patch level, the expected downtime, and the backout procedure summary. Customers may reply with a documented objection within the notice period; unresolved objections are escalated to the Head of Infrastructure.

## 5 Backout

Every patch job requires a documented backout plan before the window opens. Acceptable backout methods are:

- Configuration restore from the configuration vault for software and configuration changes.
- Image rollback for major version upgrades where a previous image is retained on the device.

No change may proceed without an approved backout plan. The Service Desk verifies the backout plan is present in the change record before the window opens. A window without a documented backout is automatically cancelled.

Backout testing must confirm the device is operational and customer-facing services are restored. The duty engineer records the result in the change record.

## 6 Testing

All patches are applied to the staging lab at DC1 before production deployment. The staging lab mirrors the production topology for the device family being patched.
